class_data.name: Spellcasting
class_data.notes:
You have learned to cast spells through prayer and meditation.

Cantrips. You know three cantrips of your choice from the Cleric spell list. Guidance, Sacred Flame, and Thaumaturgy are recommended. Whenever you gain a Cleric level, you can replace one of your cantrips with another Cleric cantrip of your choice. At Cleric levels 4 and 10, you learn one additional cantrip, as shown in the Cantrips column of the Cleric Features table.

Spell Slots. The Cleric Features table shows how many spell slots you have for your level 1+ spells. You regain all expended spell slots when you finish a Long Rest.

Prepared Spells of Level 1+. You prepare a list of Cleric spells of level 1+ that you can cast. To start, choose four level 1 Cleric spells. Bless, Cure Wounds, Guiding Bolt, and Shield of Faith are recommended. The number of prepared spells increases with your Cleric level, as shown in the Prepared Spells column of the Cleric Features table. Prepared spells must be of levels for which you have spell slots. If a Cleric feature gives you spells that are always prepared, they don’t count against this number but are still Cleric spells for you.

Changing Prepared Spells. When you finish a Long Rest, you can change your prepared list, replacing any number of prepared spells with other Cleric spells for which you have spell slots.

Spellcasting Ability. Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for your Cleric spells.

Spellcasting Focus. You can use a Holy Symbol as a Spellcasting Focus for your Cleric spells.

class_data.name: Divine Order
class_data.notes:
You dedicate yourself to one sacred role: Protector or Thaumaturge, gaining benefits based on your choice.

Protector. You gain proficiency with Martial weapons and training with Heavy armor.

Thaumaturge. You know one extra Cleric cantrip. In addition, you add your Wisdom modifier (minimum +1) as a bonus to your Intelligence (Arcana or Religion) checks.

class_data.name: Channel Divinity
class_data.notes:
You can use Channel Divinity to fuel magical effects, such as Divine Spark and Turn Undead. You can use this class’s Channel Divinity twice, regaining one use on a Short Rest and all uses on a Long Rest. At higher levels, you gain additional uses as shown in the Channel Divinity column of the Cleric Features table. Channel Divinity save DCs use your Cleric spell save DC.

Divine Spark. As a Magic action, you target a creature within 30 feet and roll 1d8 + your Wisdom modifier. You either heal that amount or force the target to make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, it takes Necrotic or Radiant damage (your choice) equal to the total; on a success, it takes half as much damage, rounded down. The damage increases to 2d8 + your Wisdom modifier at level 7, 3d8 + your Wisdom modifier at level 13, and 4d8 + your Wisdom modifier at level 18.

Turn Undead. As a Magic action, you present your Holy Symbol and choose any number of Undead within 30 feet of yourself. Each chosen Undead must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the creature is Frightened and Incapacitated for up to 1 minute and must use its movement to move away from you on its turns. The effect ends early if the creature takes any damage, if you become Incapacitated, or if you die.

class_data.name: Subclass Feature
class_data.notes: You gain a Cleric Subclass, which grants additional features at various Cleric levels.

class_data.name: Ability Score Improvement
class_data.notes: You gain an Ability Score Improvement or a feat of your choice. You gain this feature again at levels 8, 12, and 16.

class_data.name: Sear Undead
class_data.notes: Whenever you use Turn Undead, roll a number of d8s equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of 1d8). Each Undead that fails its saving throw against that use of Turn Undead takes Radiant damage equal to the total rolled. This damage does not end the Turn Undead effect.

class_data.name: Subclass Feature
class_data.notes: You gain a feature from your Cleric Subclass.

class_data.name: Blessed Strikes
class_data.notes:
You gain one of the following options: Divine Strike or Potent Spellcasting.

Divine Strike. Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can cause the attack to deal an extra 1d8 Necrotic or Radiant damage (your choice).

Potent Spellcasting. You add your Wisdom modifier to the damage you deal with any Cleric cantrip.

class_data.name: Ability Score Improvement
class_data.notes: You gain an Ability Score Improvement or a feat of your choice.

class_data.name: Divine Intervention
class_data.notes: As a Magic action, you choose a Cleric spell of level 5 or lower that does not require a Reaction and cast it without expending a spell slot or needing Material components. Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

subclass_data.name: Light Domain Spells
subclass_data.notes: You always have the listed spells prepared at the appropriate Cleric levels. See spell_table.

subclass_data.name: Radiance of the Dawn
subclass_data.notes: As a Magic action, expend Channel Divinity to create a 30-foot light burst. Magical Darkness in the area is dispelled. Each creature you choose in the area makes a Constitution save, taking Radiant damage equal to 2d10 + your Cleric level (half on success).

subclass_data.name: Warding Flare
subclass_data.notes: When a creature within 30 feet makes an attack roll, you can take a Reaction to impose Disadvantage by flaring light. Uses equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum 1), restored on a Long Rest.

subclass_data.name: Improved Warding Flare
subclass_data.notes: You regain all Warding Flare uses on a Short or Long Rest. Whenever you use Warding Flare, the target of the triggering attack gains Temporary Hit Points equal to 2d6 + your Wisdom modifier.

effects.name: Resourceful
effects.notes: You gain Heroic Inspiration whenever you finish a Long Rest.

effects.name: Skillful
effects.notes: You gain proficiency in one skill of your choice.

effects.name: Versatile
effects.notes: You gain an Origin feat of your choice.

feats.notes: Initiative Proficiency. When you roll Initiative, you can add your Proficiency Bonus to the roll.Initiative Swap. Immediately after you roll Initiative, you can swap your Initiative with the Initiative of one willing ally in the same combat. You can't make this swap if you or the ally has the Incapacitated condition.
feats.name: Alert

feats.notes: Cook's Utensils. You gain proficiency with Cook's Utensils if you don't already have it.Replenishing Meal. As part of a Short Rest, you can cook special food if you have ingredients and Cook's Utensils on hand. You can prepare enough of this food for a number of creatures equal to 4 plus your Proficiency Bonus. At the end of the Short Rest, any creature who eats the food and spends one or more Hit Dice to regain Hit Points regains an extra 1d8 Hit Points.Bolstering Treats. With 1 hour of work or when you finish a Long Rest, you can cook a number of treats equal to your Proficiency Bonus if you have ingredients and Cook's Utensils on hand. These special treats last 8 hours after being made. A creature can use a Bonus Action to eat one of those treats to gain a number of Temporary Hit Points equal to your Proficiency Bonus.
feats.name: Chef

feats.notes: Energy Mastery. Choose one of the following damage types: Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Thunder. Spells you cast ignore Resistance to damage of the chosen type. In addition, when you roll damage for a spell you cast that deals damage of that type, you can treat any 1 on a damage die as a 2.
feats.name: Elemental Adept
